sections.content:
Introduces macroeconomic problems and the corresponding model starting from the Long run, then medium run and the short run.

Except for the Long Run Solow model, all the remaining models: Neo classical and the New Keynesian (sticky price) model are derived based on micro-foundation.

i.e. start from deriving individual and firms optimizing behavioural functions, such as consumption, investment functions, and then equaling demand and supply in the economy to achieve the general equilibrium outcome.

After that, we will play with the model and try to see how the model react to different exogenous economic shocks. Then we compare models' prediction with empirical data to evaluate the model.

In summary, most part of the course is the backstory of the AS-AD model taught in DSE econ.

The course uses tools we learned in Econ 3113, but does not focus
as much on abstract content.

In my opinion, it is an interesting Econ course, because economic intuition is emphasized rather than cruching numbers. You still need to understand the FOC conditions (MB = MC) tho, that's also part of the intuition.
sections.teaching:
Jenny will derive all equations, formulas and graphs during class with us. Sometimes its hard to follow her derivation and think through the intuition behind the formulas simultaneously as her writing speed is so fast. Luckily she would upload hand-written notes and lecture videos afterwards (not immediately after class). So better focus on her explanation in class first in case you get lost.

For the class participation, even though you miss the IPRS session which are usually held rightafter class begins, Jenny will do another session for the latecomers. IPRS sessions are only graded in terms of participation not on correctness.

Tutorial is taught by Astor:
She is a nice person and is willing to answer your questions f2f or through email.
Some tutorials are used for reviewing assignments and some are used for practicing textbooks questions.
She will mention the key points she looks for when she grades exam, so its worthy to stay attentive during tutorial.

sections.content:
Prof Qiu used 5 big slides to cover all topics this semester:
1. Solow growth model
2. Micro foundation: consumption-saving, labor-leisure on individual side, wage-labor on firm side, market-clear condition, all those combinations in endowment and production economy. This part emphasizes a lot on algebra. It is important to understand which side the question is asking u.
—Midterm exam—
3. Medium run Neoclassical model: economy under flexible price
4. Short run New Keynesian model: extension on Neoclassical model, including AD-AS in partial/fully sticky price
5. Two-period New Keynesian model: NOT related to textbook, prof derived it himself. Use formula to explain AD-AS and some real-world application.
—Final exam—

- Final exam is not cumulative, only covers slides 4 and 5. Slide 3 is never covered in exam as it is more like a foundation for AD-AS.

- Prof didn’t teach open economy this semester. Instead, he spared more time for review. He used more than 2 sessions each time before midterm/final.

- The content before and after midterm is quite different in my view. Before midterm, math derivation is very very tedious. But after midterm, curve movement and qualitative analysis is more emphasized. Therefore, it doesn't matter if u did bad in midterm.
sections.teaching:
I can see Prof’s passion on economics and he is trying to make his content more easy to understand each time before his class. However, his teaching is really hard to follow.

For math derivation, he never used pen to write down any annotation on slides and just talked about the key steps. I can feel he had the big picture in his brain, but I couldn’t get the message. Although he would add on further explanation based on students’ questions in the next class, it sometimes involved many amendments on slides, which made me more confused about the structure.

For graph analysis (AD-AS), I think it would be more helpful to draw something to show the curve changes. But Prof seldom did so.

BUT his review before exam was still valuable. Especially for the final, his plan on designing the exam is very consistent with what was actually tested in exam. I think it’s an improvement, as I had no idea on the questions in midterm.

- Participation is about occasional IPRS questions. Prof only adopted it in November for 4 times, and as long as u did 3 times, u would get full marks. He reminded everyone he would do IPRS in the next class, and didn't check attendance on Friday 9am class so that students can skip it, which was really considerate.

My score after revision: 59/100 (below mean 1 SD)

My score: 98/100

Final Grade: A-

Prof said students should get around 85 something if they aim A range, with some variation in each year. I think the cutoff raises this semester probably because the final is designed much easier than last year, and most of the students get full participation bonus (which made it indifferent to introduce bonus). Therefore, I won't say it's "Good grade", but his continuous adjustment on difficulty level and style on exam throughout the semester can be a chance to fix a tragedy in midterm.

He will ask questions in a short sentence instead of giving clear guidance. He improved it in the final, adding an explanation note to clarify what he wanted to ask.

I suggest reading textbook to understand the concepts. It is very helpful.

sections.content: This is a quantitative macroeconomics course that uses multivariable calculus to derive results to prove economic intuitions. Topics cover LR solow model, microfoundation, MR and SR.
sections.teaching: Prof Qiu is a nice person. He prepares extensive lecture notes prior to lectures. His background is insane, Renmin University and Penn PhD! He teaches slowly and is willing to answer our questions. This is his first time teaching intermediate macro theory, so once in a while he might include something a bit difficult to digest. Remember to read the GLS book, it has everything you need to know about this course.
sections.grading: Absolute grading. The final exam was more difficult than he had planned and he adjusted the cutoffs. Overall of 60 would probably yield an A-. I think it is fair for a 3113-43 series course.
sections.workload: Workload is minimal. There are four problem sets. I quote him “please write something even if you are not sure so we can give you full score”. The TA Emily is brilliant at explaining the questions. There are only one attendance check and he made the announcement one week in advance.

sections.content:
** Syllabus Change After 2021 Fall **

第二個macro course，老實講我唔太鍾意個content，佢係3123嘅extension，即係加野落ISLM同release一啲assumptions。但係佢好似好多野都好夾硬嚟，讀完如果有人問你點睇香港未來嘅經濟，你就可以答：唔知架，睇下啲人點expect個government同central bank做野囉，或者要加啲好strong嘅assumptions落去。同埋可能我本身麻麻地macro，所以我係極認同啲人話咩macro姐係A+B=C，所以C-A=B，對我嚟講好似無咩有趣嘅地方。但個course overall嚟講唔算難，亦唔算多野，只係兩個新model only，仲要互不相關，係要熟啲野only。

數學嚟講好似反而無3123咁多algebra，重點嘅位反而係個concept同埋某個variable會點樣郁條ISLM之類。唯一重數嘅位就係講expectation augmented ISLM嘅時候會用utility maximization去做microfoundation推個新consumption function出嚟，所以可能會用少少3113嘅知識，但其實都只係普通mul cal，唔使太擔心。反而呢個course考試同功課都係寫字多。至於洗唔洗讀完3113先讀呢個course就見仁見智啦，佢就唔係佔好多架姐。但係3123嘅野就要記清楚啲ISLMPC同solow model都會無啦啦出現返。

Course content:
1. Expectation augmented ISLM （擺埋uncertainty同expectation落去個model做analysis)
  1.1. Financial market and expectation （講expectation點樣影響stock price/bond price嗰啲，如果熟finance會好啲）
  1.2. Expectation, consumption and investment (用expectation重新寫C同I個function form，要用少少3113嘅野）
  1.3. Expectation, output and policy （全部野放返落ISLM到，佢會話個expectation即係medium run同long run outcome，要用ISLMPC同solow predict個outcome再放返落short run ISLM到，極麻煩）

--------------------midterm----------------------

2. Exchange rate and open economy (另一個model，學同前面一啲關係都無，考試都係non-cumulative）
  2.1. Openness in goods and financial markets (基本上就係放返export同import入去，同埋講下Balance of Payment，讀過DSE應該完全無難度）
  2.2. Goods market in an open economy （擺返落Y=Z到，同埋加埋NX curve去做analysis，好鍾意問咩policy mix可以back to potential output又improve trade balance）
  2.3. Output, the interest rates, the exchange rate in the short run （擺埋exchange rate落去，記住UIRP condition就完咗了，我懷疑因為我地assume LM 打橫，所以呢part極奇怪）
  2.4. Exchange rate regimes （講下fixed exchange rate個trillemma同fixed同floating各有咩好壞）

3. Back to policy (時代革命所以成個cut咗）
  3.1. Fiscal policy
  3.2. Monetary policy
sections.teaching:
Jenny絕對好過Lu Yang，at least佢真係識啲野，但都只係普普通通，佢每堂都係會用powerpoint啦，同埋都用visualizer喺紙上面寫啲notes，同埋microfoundation嗰part textbook係無嘅，一定要聽佢講。overall嚟講無咩同學生交流，咁好似同佢開sem嗰時堅持要小班個原意有啲唔同。英文都唔算差，有好少少accent，但唔影響聽。另外個course有個幾大嘅問題就係你可以明晒佢上堂講嘅野但係唔識考試，因為佢啲題目都幾多ambiguity，題題個答案都好似係uncertain咁，所以midterm前有極多人衝上去問佢姐係點答，佢好似講到好唔耐煩，叫我地盡量寫，有得吹就吹（其實都真係要咁）。

tutor係astor，佢其實個教學質素都幾參差，去到一定要多啲math嘅topic佢好似就唔係好掂，但普通一啲conceptual嘅野佢反而講得唔錯，有時都會同我地吹下水，又會教下我地點考試點去做份project，好過佢3123嗰陣，不過第一堂同3123第一堂係一模一樣- -又撳啲data網。
sections.grading:
我估佢都會係比較靚grade，唔會太差。但未出grade就純文字討論住，應該2月中先會出grade，而可能大家都諗緊下個sem會唔會reg呢個course，就寫住先。啲考試同埋problem set個設計基本上係一模一樣，又係True False with explanation，short questions，math questions，essay咁樣落去。

Grading System:
Problem sets 18%
Midterm exam 30%
Group Project 10.5%
       Final Report (8%)
       Presentation (2%)
       Peer evaluation (0.5%)
Final exam 40%
Class participation 1.5% (係個謎，無人知佢點俾分）

Grading System (時代革命版，揀高分啲嗰個scheme）：
Problem sets 18%
Midterm exam 30%
Group Project 20.5%
       Final Report (16%)
       Presentation (4%)
       Peer evaluation (0.5%)
Final exam 30%
Class participation 1.5%
sections.workload:
好重workload下個course。佢啲problem set就3份，以一個sem得三份啲講，其實每份你話長又唔係真係好長。但係每題你都要時間諗，而且要寫一抽幾長下嘅答案去答。但好就好在astor淨係會抽幾題出嚟改，跟住由100分開始扣起，錯晒都分分鐘有九十幾分。

Exam就non-cumulative，所以相對地係比較輕鬆，唔使用咁多時間去溫，但真係要熟每個detail位，佢係會考到幾detail下。

Project就6-7個人一組，跟住佢俾10個topic大家去搶。但佢個topic極闊，例如咩internationalization of RMB，可能大家要做就要focus返喺background同埋啲Policy阿之類，同埋用返啲model同real data support啲effect of policy/ financial crisis。佢話就話要交咩reading同埋要用regression去做data analysis，但我個人覺得有啲太多，大家當寫篇野做個introduction其實就得，當然你aim high可以搵個啱嘅methodology去做analysis，做之前問下Jenny咁樣o唔ok。 sem尾就要搵兩條友去present 20分鐘同交一篇3000字左右嘅paper。如果無人freeride都唔算太難嘅，但sem尾會幾大壓力。

sections.content: You could learn a lot of practical and useful macroeconomics knowledge (e.g. growth theories, exchange rate, open economy...) in this course. However, the course materials were not easy and I needed to spend a lot of time to fully understand all of them.
sections.teaching: Teaching style was fair. Professor included a lot of real world examples and topics (e.g. RMB internationalization) which were quite interesting.
sections.grading: Problem Sets (21.5%) + Midterm (30%) + Final (45%) + Parti (3.5%). Problems sets were not difficult and Parti was easy to get full mark given that you attended all the lessons. As a result, you grade was actually solely depended on the exams. To score high marks, you really had to fully understand and remember all the concepts (revise the notes after each lessons and every weekend) which was not an easy task. Most people got B range in this course. Mainland students didn't have much advantages in this course as this course tested concepts more than calculus. My final grade: A.
sections.workload: The explicit workload was not high (problem sets + exams only). However, if you want to get A range, you do have to spend quite a lot of time to understand all the concepts. Don't underestimate the difficulty of this course.

sections.content: Mainly theories with some rmb real examples. Little maths. Notes are pretty enough to understand the topics. Some questions in the assignments may be tested so read the notes and assignments thoroughly before you sit for an exam.
sections.teaching:
Like most of the lecturers, she taught the lesson using powerpont, but she also writes down the important things on papers and demonstrate how to draw graphs. She is well-prepared for every lessons.

The professor is very nice. If you find any problems you can just drop her an email and she must reply you and answer you questions.
sections.grading: The grading is good in general. I know some students having an average midterm but a below-mean final and he finally got B, so it seems that the grading scheme is not too strict in this course.
sections.workload: The workload is appropriate. There are four assignments in total and about 5% for each assignment. But the marking schemes for the assignments are not strict at all, so it's easy to get high marks for assignments. No projects and presentations.

sections.content: Pretty boring staff. All about theory. Basically no math. All concept staff. Pay attention to what she talked about in the last few lectures which is not in the textbook. They will be tested in the exam for sure.
sections.teaching: The teacher try to cultivate our interest in economics, but her class is just as boring as the other mainland female economics teachers. Basically if you read the textbook you can predict the next sentence she will say.
sections.grading: Very bad. I heard two people got D and one got fail in this course. This course is exclusive for Ecof and Maec students, and I cannot believe the grading scale is so bad. All Gbus and Qfin exclusive courses have very generous grading scale, but ECOF courses are all grade killers.
sections.workload: Workload is OK. Several homework assignments, one midterm and one final exam. Participation is all based on whether she could recognize your face or not.
